notice: RN bank batch 35: Pharmacology II: psychiatric medications and drug safety. DRAFT - every question must be reviewed by an RN or nurse educator before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client recently started sertraline and also takes tramadol. The client is agitated and sweating, with a temperature of 39 °C (102.2 °F), muscle twitching and hyperactive reflexes. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: Serotonin syndrome: stop the serotonergic drugs and give supportive care; cyproheptadine may be used.

perOption.a: Combining serotonergic drugs causes agitation, hyperthermia, clonus and hyperreflexia.
perOption.b: NMS causes rigid muscles and slow reflexes, usually with antipsychotics.
perOption.c: This causes dry, hot skin, not sweating with clonus.
perOption.d: This doesn't cause hyperthermia and clonus.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.stem: A client started fluoxetine 1 week ago and says, "It's not working, so I'll stop it." What is the best response?

options.text: "It can take 2 to 6 weeks to feel the full effect. Please keep taking it and talk with your provider."

rationale.correct: Antidepressants: delayed effect, watch for suicidal thoughts early on, don't stop abruptly.

perOption.a: SSRIs take weeks to work; stopping suddenly can cause discontinuation symptoms.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
DRAFT: original question written with AI assistance; an RN or nurse educator must check it before candidates rely on it.

questions.educationalObjective: Teach about the delayed effect of SSRIs.

questions.stem: A client taking phenelzine (an MAOI) plans a meal. Which food choice shows a need for more teaching?

rationale.correct: MAOIs: avoid tyramine (aged cheese, cured meats, tap beer, soy sauce) and many drug interactions.

perOption.a: Tyramine-rich foods can cause a hypertensive crisis with MAOIs.
perOption.b: Fresh meat is low in tyramine.
perOption.d: Fresh cheeses are low in tyramine.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: A client taking lithium has a level of 2.1 mEq/L, with coarse tremors, vomiting and confusion. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Hold the lithium and notify the provider right away
Document the findings and recheck tomorrow

rationale.correct: Lithium: therapeutic about 0.6 to 1.2 mEq/L; keep sodium and fluid intake steady; watch for toxicity.

perOption.a: A level above about 1.5 mEq/L with these symptoms indicates toxicity.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

options.text: "I'll keep my salt and fluid intake about the same every day."
"I'll skip my blood tests if I feel fine."

rationale.correct: Lithium: steady sodium and fluids, avoid NSAIDs and diuretics, regular blood levels.

perOption.a: Changes in sodium and fluids alter lithium levels.

questions.stem: A client who started haloperidol 2 days ago has a temperature of 40 °C (104 °F), severe muscle rigidity, confusion and an unstable blood pressure. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: NMS: stop the antipsychotic, cool the client, give supportive care and possibly dantrolene or bromocriptine.

perOption.a: This is a life-threatening reaction to antipsychotics.
perOption.b: This develops after long-term use and involves involuntary movements.
perOption.d: That causes clonus and is linked to serotonergic drugs.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: For each finding in a client taking an antipsychotic, indicate the adverse effect.

rows.text: Sudden, painful neck spasm with the eyes rolled upward
Shuffling gait, tremor and a masklike face
Lip smacking and tongue thrusting after years of treatment

rationale.correct: Acute dystonia is treated with an anticholinergic such as diphenhydramine or benztropine; screen for TD with the AIMS.

perOption.r1:c1: This is an acute dystonic reaction.
perOption.r1:c3: This is a sudden spasm, not tremor or rigidity.
perOption.r2:c2: Akathisia is restlessness and an inability to sit still.
perOption.r4:c4: TD causes involuntary facial movements after long-term use.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

options.text: Hold the dose and check the white blood cell and absolute neutrophil counts
Give acetaminophen and continue the drug

rationale.correct: Clozapine: monitor the ANC regularly; also watch for seizures, myocarditis and metabolic effects.

questions.stem: A client with depression is prescribed a large supply of amitriptyline. What is the nurse's main safety concern?

options.text: Tricyclic antidepressants are highly lethal in overdose because of cardiac dysrhythmias

rationale.correct: TCAs: anticholinergic effects, orthostatic hypotension and cardiotoxicity in overdose.

perOption.a: Prescribe limited amounts for clients at risk of suicide.

rationale.correct: Valproate: liver tests, platelets, pancreatitis risk and birth defects (avoid in pregnancy).

perOption.a: Valproate can cause hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis.

perOption.a: Lamotrigine can cause Stevens-Johnson syndrome; any rash needs evaluation.

questions.stem: An 84-year-old is prescribed diphenhydramine for sleep. Why should the nurse question this?

options.text: Its anticholinergic effects can cause confusion, urinary retention and falls in older adults
It is ineffective in older adults

rationale.correct: Avoid strongly anticholinergic drugs in older adults when possible.

perOption.a: It is on the Beers list of drugs to avoid in older adults.
perOption.d: The concern is harm, not effectiveness.

references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information

questions.stem: Which statement shows a client understands safe acetaminophen use?

options.text: "I'll check the labels of cold medicines because many contain acetaminophen too."
"I can take as much as I want because it's over-the-counter."
"I'll take extra if my fever doesn't go down."

rationale.correct: Acetaminophen: usually no more than 3 to 4 g a day for healthy adults (less with liver disease or alcohol use); watch for hidden sources.

perOption.a: Hidden acetaminophen in combination products causes accidental overdose.
perOption.d: Doses must stay within the limit.

perOption.a: ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics together raise the risk of hyperkalemia.

perOption.a: Many antibiotics, including ciprofloxacin, increase warfarin's effect.

questions.stem: A client who takes simvastatin asks about grapefruit juice. What is the best response?

options.text: "Avoid large amounts of grapefruit; it can raise simvastatin levels and the risk of muscle damage."
"Take the statin with grapefruit juice for best absorption."

rationale.correct: Grapefruit interacts with some statins, calcium channel blockers and immunosuppressants.

perOption.a: Grapefruit inhibits CYP3A4, which metabolizes simvastatin.

questions.stem: Two weeks after starting allopurinol, a client has a widespread rash with blisters, fever and sores in the mouth. What does the nurse suspect?

rationale.correct: SJS: stop the drug right away; it is linked to allopurinol, sulfonamides, lamotrigine and anticonvulsants.

perOption.a: This is a severe skin reaction that needs the drug stopped and emergency care.
perOption.b: This doesn't cause fever and mouth sores.

questions.stem: A client becomes very agitated, and the provider orders IM haloperidol and lorazepam. What is the nurse's priority after giving them?

options.text: Monitor airway, breathing, blood pressure and level of sedation
Leave the client alone to rest
Give the next dose in 15 minutes

rationale.correct: After emergency sedation, monitor vital signs, airway and EPS closely.

perOption.a: The combination can cause sedation, hypotension and respiratory depression.
